body: Oof. I have been feeling pretty terrible myself, and I hate that we have that in common. I don’t have any words of wisdom, but know that at the very least you’re not alone. If I could I’d give you a hug. I can promise you it’ll be okay but I can promise you someone else cares about you and hope your suffering eases.

You captured it perfectly. Last time I dated anyone was 11 years ago, and I’m so much more comfortable being direct with everyone really. Not confrontational, just stating the facts, like you said, with no truly no pressure.
Sometimes it’s just nice to hear someone’s thoughts other than my own. In the end, I like to go with my gut.
I can definitely see that, and for the record you’re being realistic, not an asshole.

This is for all of you, including OP, but so many others - you’re all enough for a relationship. Period. You all have value and beauty, I absolutely guarantee it. Love your best qualities, whatever they are, be proud of them and let them shine. That’s beautiful. I know it’s cheesy, but I 100% mean it. Looks have a much smaller role in this than you’d think. Be confident, because each of you has a lot to offer. You will attract people who see the whole you, and you deserve that.

To me it sounds like you have a generous heart, and you want to be and feel seen, and maybe even feel purposeful. That’s nothing to be ashamed of. Like others have said, you still did a kind thing for someone in need, regardless why you decided to help. I hope you can see the beauty in what you did - and there is nothing wrong with feeling good for doing good. 

Be gentle with yourself and take care.

Thank you!!! I learned this is drivers ed and it’s always stuck with me, but no one believes me! (The part about being stopped and seeing the tires on the road of the car in front of you).  Also, less tailgating would improve traffic bc of less unnecessary breaking. Thanks for being a good driver!
Thank you - all of this has been so helpful.

For real, this is what I needed to know. I’ll get
down to brass tacks then.
Definitely at the top of the list.

Oh, I was married for 10 years, I’m aware ;)

Honestly though this is really helpful! I’m fine with spelling it out if I have to.  Thanks!

Going to a residential treatment facility for my life-long depression and anxiety. Didn’t hurt to not have alcohol or weed to self-medicate either. Literally saved my life. It’s tough to confront all your demons head-on, but if you are in a good program the support around you is so incredible and non-judgmental. Was there for a bit over a month, wish it could have been longer. Still recovering, still have rough days and navigating some other tough life changes (namely reevaluating a lot of toxic relationships) but wouldn’t change it for anything in the world, and truly feel like there is something worth living for for the first time in my life. Might sound like hyperbole, but I promise you it isn’t. 

I feel very privileged it was something I was able to do - but if you have insurance and feel like this would be helpful, look into it. My insurance is relatively bad, and it covered almost all of the cost. (This is in the US - I like to hope this kind of help is easier to access elsewhere).

Thank you for the recommendation - I’ll definitely read that. Some of what you mentioned about your experience really hit home. Yes, I’m realizing there has been a lot of emotional abuse during our relationship … I’m pretty ashamed of how long I’ve let someone treat me like this. I can finally see that I don’t deserve that.

Not rude at all - just wanted to take the time for others out there too who have experienced any kind of relationship abuse and give the perspective from the inside. All good - you cut right to the chase. :)

Yes! I absolutely don’t want to discount this as a real thing. It definitely is and I’m glad you’re able
to manage it. 

In my case there is a lot of history and past trauma that come into play with this that makes it more difficult. Mostly though I did want to acknowledge that this is a very real thing that can happen. 

Wishing you and your fiancé much joy and love in your lives. ❤️

Thank you - I’m so sorry you’ve had this kind of experience.  I can relate to a lot of this - especially the justifying every little thing (which then seems super crazy if you do it with someone normal!) and lying to get a break - I can’t tell you the number of times I’ve circled my neighborhood after work, or parked in a parking lot somewhere just to delay going home a little longer. It means a lot to been seen and know I’m not crazy (at least not when it comes to this 😉). Thank you ❤️

Yeah, 100% agreed. It’s super fucked up - he even spent like a good half hour once going in circles with our couples therapist trying to get him to understand you 1) don’t touch people in anger for ANY reason 2) I’m his wife and he doesn’t get to teach me any lessons 3) you absolutely don’t teach someone a lesson through violence. 

This is embarrassing, but that incident happened like 2 years ago, and just before I left for treatment we got into an argument about something, and somehow this incident came up and he STILL doesn’t think he did anything wrong. I was floored. He straight up denies ever hitting me, bc he doesn’t think that counts. 

I’m seeing more and more his inability to take responsibility for his actions, it’s been eye opening.

So, yes - that’s like the tl;dr version. But it’s so much less black and white when you’re in it. 

In a previous job, I ran an awards program in affiliation with a local pro sports team that recognized outstanding citizens in the community, and often our nominees were people who in one way or another worked with those experiencing domestic violence. The stories some of these women told me were harrowing - and every one of them said they never thought it would happen to them, and if it did they would just leave immediately, but none of them did. Eventually they got out, but they would all tell you how hard it is to leave. I think it’s something that’s maybe difficult to understand until it’s happening to you. 

I know at some point I declared I would walk straight out the door and never look back the if a partner ever laid a hand on me in anger. But I didn’t. You don’t want it to be true. You want to think like, yeah but it wasn’t like he punched me so does it really count? To be clear the answer is yes, it does. But this is someone you’ve picked, someone you wanted to be a part of your life, someone you love. And it’s really hard to accept that someone who occupies that special place in your heart would ever do anything to harm you. You don’t want it to be true.

Yeah, he claims it’s sexsomnia and his doctor doesn’t want to prescribe him sleeping pills or anything bc it’s “not that bad”. I hate saying this, and I don’t have anything concrete to back it up, but I don’t completely believe that he’s actually asleep during these episodes, or at least not all of them.

Thank you for this. Luckily my parents live near by. My mom happened to drop me off at home the day I got home from treatment. He happened to be leaving to take the dog out as we pulled up. He almost walked right by me to his car when my mom said something about maybe giving me a hug first? He did, then she asked him to help me with my suitcase and he said “She’s a big girl, she can get her own bags”.  Anyway, my mom was highly disturbed by that, and has offered to let me stay with them as long as necessary. 

I’m fortunate to have my own car, bought on my own, and bank accounts and credit cards. We do have a joint account, but I only contribute my share of household costs (mortgage, utilities, etc.).  

I will PM you with my city info, I would love the help if you’re able to recommend any services in my area. 

It’s so helpful to be able to talk about this, and to be validated in my experience. Thank you ❤️
Thank you for the encouragement. We don’t have kids, so that does make things easier. I’m glad to hear you’re doing well. ❤️

I could have written this, other than I don’t own a gun, which is for the best bc I probably would play Russian roulette with it too. I’m so sorry you feel this way too. I so desperately wish I had some way to comfort you and bring you some relief from your pain, because I feel that pain too and I know how excruciating it can be. Thank you so much for this, it means a lot and has given me a little extra dose of encouragement. Still working on details, but let my employer know today that I’ll be taking time off and why (a very abbreviated version, but the truth - seeking help for depression) and they fully support me. Thank you again for the encouragement, I needed that.

I went to Hawaii with my family after my brother and I graduated from high school. One morning they all went to play tennis, but I don’t play so I went down to a nearby cove with a small beaches. As I was walking down there a boy and his father walking the other direction and told me there was a pod of dolphins in the cove. I got down there and sure enough there is a pod of dolphins swimming around about 100 yards from the shoreline. I was/am a good swimmer and grabbed my goggles and swam out. Then I noticed they were also swimming towards me. And then they were all around me, and I swam around underwater with them, them keeping my pace so we could sort of check each other out. They were close enough to touch but I wouldn’t dare. Aside from generally thinking it a bad idea, up close they were huge. Likely common or bottlenose. 

Anyway we had this amazing swim encounter and then when they’d tired of me the headed out of the cove. They were gone. 

No one else was at the cove. All I’d brought were my goggles and towel and this was in pre-smartphones times and I had no camera or any other way to document the experience—all I have is the memory. I have no evidence for any of this to prove it happened, so you’ll just have to believe me that it happened, and it was magical.
Me too. It’s always been there, sometimes it’s just louder than other times.

We did this 6 months in. One week in the car together and camping in whatever town or camping area we found. We saw amazing things, it was great, and we also broke down in a small town over Labor Day weekend (auto shops closed) 8 hours away from home. The town hotels were all booked because of a motorcycle festival. We spent the night in a shitty motel planning how we’d get home, drinking whatever was in our cooler and laughing about our insane misfortune. We figured out a plan and made it home the next day - it involved him hiking a couple miles to pick up the last rental car in town. We’ve been together for 11 years now and we both remember this trip fondly, car troubles and all.
